sources.note: Ba, Kiros & Hinton 2016 — LayerNorm; the panel's x, mean, variance, and output values are the chapter's worked example.
Zhang & Sennrich 2019 — RMSNorm; the panel's root-mean-square value and output are the chapter's.
Xiong et al. 2020 — post-norm gradient instability and warmup; the lane's pre-norm/post-norm Jacobian comparison follows the chapter.

figures.title: LayerNorm centers; RMSNorm only scales
figures.caption: LayerNorm subtracts the token's mean and divides by its standard deviation; RMSNorm divides by the root mean square and keeps the sign. On x = [2, 4, 6, 8], LayerNorm's output has mean 0 and standard deviation 1, while RMSNorm's output has mean 0.913 and is not centered.
figures.alt: Two aligned panels. LayerNorm: x = 2, 4, 6, 8; mean 5; centered -3, -1, 1, 3; variance 5 and standard deviation 2.236; output -1.342, -0.447, 0.447, 1.342 with mean 0 and standard deviation 1. RMSNorm: the same x; mean of squares 30; root mean square 5.477; output 0.365, 0.730, 1.095, 1.461 with mean 0.913, so it is not centered.

panels.title: LayerNorm
panels.note: Invariant to adding a constant; scale-invariant up to ε.

panels.title: RMSNorm
panels.note: Invariant to scaling, not to shifting.

figures.title: Pre-norm keeps the identity path outside the norm
figures.caption: In a pre-norm block the normalization sits inside each sublayer's input and the residual addition stays outside it, so the identity path above the stages is not multiplied by a normalization Jacobian. Post-norm moves the normalization after the addition, putting J_LN on that path; that is the path that needs warmup.
figures.alt: A lane with six stages: LN(x), attention, add x, LN(a), MLP, add a. A line above the stages marks the residual stream; both additions write to it, and in pre-norm neither addition is followed by a normalization. Labels give d_model at each normalization, 4d_model² for attention, and 8d_model² for the MLP. The note gives the pre-norm Jacobian I + J_f(LN(x)) J_LN(x) and the post-norm form J_LN (I + J_f).

data.note: Pre-norm: a = x + Attn(LN(x)); x' = a + MLP(LN(a)). The addition is outside the norm, so dy/dx = I + J_f(LN(x))·J_LN(x). Post-norm: y = LN(x + f(x)), so the identity path is multiplied by J_LN; Xiong et al. 2020 link that multiplication to the warmup requirement.

anim.intro: Press Play or Next to follow the residual path through a pre-norm block.

steps.label: Normalize x for attention; the norm is inside the sublayer input.
Attention mixes across positions and writes 4d_model² parameters.
Add to x. The bypass carries x past the norm.
Normalize the new stream state for the MLP.
The MLP writes 8d_model² parameters, one position at a time.
Add again. Post-norm would put LN after this add, on the identity path.
